reference.label: avgvisib_85s_060m_201608.lbl
reference.description: This data product is a map of the average illumination by the solar disc of the Lunar South Pole at a resolution of 60 m/pix by 60 m/pix, true at the pole in polar stereographic (spherical) projection. The calculations are based on the LOLA elevation map LDEM_85S_060M and are described in [MAZARICOETAL2011]. The values are continuous between 0 (permanent shadow) and 1, and indicate the percentage of timesteps where each pixel was sunlit (by any fraction of the solar disc). Note a scaling was applied to fit the data in the INT16 value range. This label describes an IMG file in the form of a binary resampling with pixel registration.
reference.image_description: Each sample is a binary value that indicates whether that location is in permanent shadow (DN=0, scaling to 0) or its average solar disc visibility (DN up to 25000, scaling to 1).
